result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Temporary Various
Remuneration: As per State Award
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: CAM28682

There is one central advertisement for Palliative Medicine, Advanced Training (AT) positions in New South Wales for 2027. Applicants are required to apply via this JMO ROB Recruitment platform only.

What you will be doing:
The Advanced Trainee in Palliative Medicine will provide quality healthcare to patients under supervision, while developing a broad knowledge of the principles and practice of palliative medicine and a satisfactory level of competence in palliative medicine as required for Advanced Training.

These positions will have supervision from specialist medical staff whilst undertaking learning and professional development as outlined by the Chapter of Palliative Medicine, Royal Australasian College of Physicians.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES: The duties of the Palliative Care medical officer will vary according to the particular location and context of the post; for example: 

HOSPITAL CONSULT TERM (mainly hospital consults)

Review patients as requested by other medical or surgical units (on the same day as requested or as close to the same day as possible).

Review the patient within 24 hours or as close to this as possible with an AMO from the affiliated palliative care service hours.

Communicate with other units the objectives of care and assist in resolving conflicts between therapeutic objectives of units.

Hospital Consults rotations may also involve some inpatient work.

INPATIENT TERM (mainly in-patient care)

Daily ward rounds of every patient in the unit.

Careful documentation in the case notes of patient progress (and tests, etc).

Responsibility for communication with AMO about any relevant change in patient's condition.

Fully admitting or at least examining all new admissions.

Responsible for ordering and chasing results of all appropriate investigations (either self-initiated or AMO-initiated).

Discharge planning, together with patient and paramedical staff and family.

Ensuring appropriate post-discharge follow-up.

Supervising discharge summaries and communication with the patient's general practitioner (LMO).

Liaise with and counsel the family or guardians of patient as required.

Prompt implementation of management changes suggested by senior staff.

To supervise resident medical officers or interns attached to the inpatient palliative care unit.

Liaise with external medical services, such as, General Practitioners, in a professional, succinct and courteous fashion.

COMMUNITY TERM (mainly community consults)

Notify AMO of new referrals on day of assessment

See all new referrals within 3 working days, and within 24hrs for urgent referrals

See patients with the AMO as directed

Liaise promptly with the patients general practitioner after each visit

Regularly review unstable patients in collaboration with the GP

See patients in all home settings as directed (residential homes, hostels, nursing homes) - Liaise regularly with the GPs and Care givers as appropriate to the patient - after carers-allied health-health providers

Provide systematic management of the community case load

OUTPATIENT CARE

Attendance at unit outpatient clinics

Assessment of unit patients in the emergency department
 

Enhance skills in handling problems on the telephone and deciding the situations in which this is appropriate
 

Where you will be working:
The appointing hospitals are accredited for core training in Palliative Medicine. Each centre will provide training in essential clinical aspects of Palliative Medicine. Some centres will require trainees to rotate to the other centres as part of their training. Applicants should contact the responsible person-head of department at each hospital or facility to which they are applying in order to find out more about their specific training programs in Palliative Medicine.
 

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

MBBS or equivalent, currently registered or eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia

RACP advanced trainees (Palliative Medicine and other subspecialties), Australasian Chapter of Palliative Medicine trainees, Clin. Foundations in Palliative Medicine (RACP) trainees, Faculty of Pain Medicine trainees and Family Medicine Program trainees or as detailed under Qualifications above

Completed at least four years residency since graduation

Current Drivers license

Proven satisfactory clinical performance, supported by submissions of two current referees

Demonstrated sound, effective communication skills with patients, medical and surgical colleagues and other staff

Demonstrated commitment to own personal and professional development

A professional attitude and flexibility in work role with a preparedness and ability to participate in after- hours overtime and on-call rosters and the required rotations both between services and geographical location to deliver patient care (including rural locations if applicable to the stream)

Need more information? 
 1) Click here for the Position Description 
 2) Find out more about applying for this position
For role related queries or questions contact Janeen Foffani on Janeen.Foffani@health.nsw.gov.au

Applications Close: August 4th, 2026    Click here to Apply now →

Work on high-impact growth-driven projects that influence organisational decision-making.

Provide financial insights that support capital allocation, funding and operational decision-making.

Prepare and present financial insights and reporting to support Executive and Board-level decision making.

Align long-term planning assumptions with annual budgets and quarterly forecasts.

Support treasury activities through cash flow forecasting and covenant modelling.

Collaborate with Finance and Digital Technology teams to ensure best in class systems and reporting.

Key Skills

Advanced financial modelling and forecasting capability.

Strong commercial and business acumen.

Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills.

Ability to confidently communicate financial information to a range of stakeholders.

Experience preparing insights and recommendations to support investment decisions.

Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship-building skills.

Experience with finance systems, BI tools and planning platforms.

Continuous improvement mindset with a focus on process optimisation.

What you'll bring

You are a commercially minded finance professional with a proven track record of partnering with senior stakeholder, influencing decision-making and delivering insights that drive sustainable business outcomes.

You will also need:

Chartered Accountant (CA) qualification or equivalent is essential.

CFA qualification highly regarded.

10+ years' finance experience, ideally within FP&A, corporate finance or financial modelling environments.

Proven experience building financial models in complex scenarios and presenting meaningful insights.

Experience supporting capital investment, business planning and forecasting activities.

Experience supporting treasury activities, capital funding decisions, covenant modelling or investment analysis will be highly regarded.

Strong technical capability across Excel, Power BI and planning systems.

Exposure to capital-intensive industries such as property, infrastructure, healthcare or aged care will be highly regarded.

Treehouse benefits and rewards, including discounts to 400 retail, accommodation and entertainment

A safe and healthy workplace culture

Contracts Administration Officer  
 Play a key role in supporting the successful delivery of community infrastructure and operational projects by providing contract administration, contractor payment and procurement support within a structured local government environment. 
  Your new opportunity  
 This Mackay-based opportunity sits within a collaborative Procurement team responsible for supporting contract management activities across a diverse portfolio of capital works and operational projects. Working closely with Project Managers, Finance and contractors, you will help ensure contracts are administered effectively, risks are managed appropriately, and contractor payments are processed accurately and in accordance with legislative and contractual requirements. 
 This role is well suited to a detail-oriented professional who enjoys working across multiple stakeholders, maintaining accurate records and contributing to the successful delivery of projects and procurement outcomes. 
  Your new role  
 As the Contracts Administration Officer, you will provide essential administrative and commercial support across Council's contractor management and procurement functions. 
 In this role you will: 
 
 Support the implementation and administration of contractor management processes in accordance with Council policies, procedures and standards 
 Assist Project Managers with maintaining accurate project costing records, forecasting and job costing information 
 Coordinate and assist with the assessment and preparation of contractor payment claims 
 Process contractor payments in accordance with contractual obligations and legislative timeframes 
 Assist with the assessment of variation claims, including documentation, negotiations and notifications 
 Prepare and maintain contract variations and associated contract documentation 
 Ensure all contract-related records are accurate, current and managed in accordance with record-keeping and retention requirements 
 Maintain accurate information within contracts management and financial systems 
 Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives across procurement and contractor management processes 
 Liaise effectively with Project Managers, Finance teams and contractors to support successful project delivery 
 
 This is a hands-on role where attention to detail, organisation and strong stakeholder engagement skills are critical to success. 
  What you'll need to succeed  
 You will bring strong administrative and contract management experience, along with the ability to manage competing priorities within a fast-paced project environment. 
 Key requirements include: 
 
 Experience processing invoices and contractor payment claims within required timeframes 
 Demonstrated experience in a contract administration or similar role 
 Experience using contract management and financial systems such as SAP, TechnologyOne, CiAnywhere or similar platforms 
 Strong Microsoft Office skills 
 Understanding of contract management processes, contract law and relevant legislation 
 Knowledge of the Building Industry Fairness (Security of Payment) Act 2017 
 Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining accurate documentation and records 
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships 
 Strong organisational and time management skills with the ability to manage a high-volume workload 
 
 Desirable: 
 
 Certificate III in Business Administration or a related qualification 
 Experience within Local Government or capital works environments 
 Experience supporting procurement and contractor management activities 
 Experience maintaining and reporting within corporate financial management systems 
 Knowledge of Local Government procurement legislation, policies and procedures 
 Commercial acumen and an understanding of the financial aspects of contracts 
 
  What you'll get in return  
 You'll be joining a supportive local government environment where your work directly contributes to the delivery of important projects and services for the community. 
 In return, you will enjoy: 
 
 A stable and rewarding opportunity within Local Government 
 Exposure to a broad range of infrastructure and operational projects 
 A collaborative and professional team environment 
 Opportunities to further develop procurement, contract administration and project support capabilities 
 The chance to work closely with a variety of stakeholders across Council and contractor networks 
 A role where accuracy, organisation and attention to detail are highly valued
